product_guards: Replace the report-only generic callback with a typed protected plan. Independently observe each source and destination as distinct same-host direct HTTPS typed-200 self-canonical HTML pages, with no errors, blocked hosts, redirects or noindex/none. Require exact requested/final/canonical identities and coherent duplicate snapshots. Require explicit root language, title/count and H1/count; select the actual unique H1 or unique title fallback without inventing a name.

Source evidence must identify actual empty internal link rows by literal href, resolved target, exact source identity, rel multiplicity and empty typed text/title/aria-label. Refuse conflicting/untyped proposals and unproved whole source groups. Accepted subsets name all unproved source pages and never fall back to AI or heuristic targeting.

Individual and bulk correction endpoints share the protected plan. Free-form, cached and confirmed model previews cannot bypass it. Refuse legacy generic callbacks without that plan before repository or provider access. Mechanically corrected files incur zero AI quota.

Bind source and every destination to unique nonshared literal .html routes in the repository. Check bounded current redirect configuration for both. Re-read source and destination bytes/SHA even if a file-state cache exists; attest exact canonical, language, title/H1 and selected literal links before planning. Reject nonliteral/shared/framework sources, scripts/templates in repository files, malformed attributes/structure and competing currently named links to equivalent destinations.

Finish the complete lot's source/destination/routing preflight and fresh bounded streamed public-target direct HTTPS probes before the first PUT. Match actual served source links and both metadata snapshots; refuse stale names, health, canonical fragments, uncertain routes and insufficient write budgets. No native preview/noindex exemption is added to the product.

Reuse the literal anchor parser and quoted-attribute lexer to insert only escaped aria-label, preserving href, content, comments, casing, quotes, line endings and all other bytes. Keep the 80000-byte UTF-8 limit and idempotence. SHA-guard each source write, never write the name-giving destination, and explicitly stop/report remaining files on a partial failure without claiming atomicity.

limitations: This proves only a same-host direct indexable self-canonical literal HTML subset and its protected endpoints. A real unproved destination/source remains unmodified and counted, so even this fixture's entire family is not resolved. Unknown metadata, other origins, redirects/noindex, shared/framework/nonliteral/dynamic sources and ambiguous routes refuse rather than guess.

The inserted accessible name is observed from the destination; it is neither semantic link-intent proof nor a promise of Google anchor-text interpretation. H1/title selection is not a language detector. Byte preservation cannot promise visual invariance for arbitrary CSS selecting aria-label.

Native previews remain noindex, production canonical-host context and zero raw sitemap seeds. Unlike indexability-filtered previous families, this crawler's healthy-HTML anchor family measures two to one in raw and controlled reports. The bounded owned host/header projection does not prove production indexability, deployment or customer acceptance.

Repository sources containing scripts/templates are refused. The existing fresh HTTP reader tolerates body scripts, including owned platform injection; it compares literal source/target metadata and links but does not execute and certify a dynamic DOM. The independent saved-body browser check is confined to this fixture.

Repository reads, current SHA writes, HTTP probes and future deployments are not atomic. Multi-file failures can leave an explicitly reported partial branch. Existing public-target validation is reused, not certified as a complete SSRF/DNS-rebinding audit.

No agent deployment, client onboarding, fresh real Claude integration, production recovery replay, scheduler/payment acceptance, capacity test or fresh PostgreSQL run is included. Forty-two SQLite skips remain. Three claimed families still lack exact named references, including one deliberately hidden legacy diagnostic; references are not readiness verdicts.
